It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it not the case that there is no group of those who are undetermined?
It should not be said thus … [as before] …
Is it not the case that there is an indefinite category? Yes.
If there is indeed an indefinite category, then surely you should not say this:
“All kamma is fixed. Are all kamma fixed? Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One that there are three groups:
the group fixed in falsehood, the group fixed in truth, and the undetermined group?
Yes, it was.
If three groups were indeed spoken of by the Blessed One—
“the group fixed in falsehood, the group fixed in truth, and the group not fixed”— then surely it should not be said that “all kamma is fixed.”
Is karma to be experienced in the present life fixed in the sense of being experienced in the present life?
Yes. Is it fixed in the sense of being fixed in wrongness? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that it is fixed in rightness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … .
Is kamma to be experienced upon rebirth ...
[and] kamma to be experienced in a subsequent life fixed in the sense of being experienced in a subsequent life? Yes.
Is it fixed in wrongness?
One should not say so … pe … Is it fixed in rightness?

It should not be said thus … [as before] … It should not be said that “kamma to be experienced in the present life is fixed in the sense of being experienced in the present life, and kamma to be experienced in the next life … [and so on].”
Is karma to be experienced in subsequent lives fixed in the sense of being "to be experienced in subsequent lives"? Yes.
Does karma to be experienced in the present life become karma to be experienced upon rebirth, or become karma to be experienced in subsequent lives? …pe… [and so on].
Is it the case that karma to be experienced upon rebirth becomes karma to be experienced in this very life, or becomes karma to be experienced in a subsequent life? ...
[and so on] ... Is it the case that karma to be experienced in a subsequent life becomes karma to be experienced in this very life, or becomes karma to be experienced upon rebirth?
One should certainly not say so.
Therefore, indeed, karma to be experienced in the present life is fixed in the sense of being experienced in the present life; karma to be experienced upon rebirth...
[and so on] ...karma to be experienced in subsequent lives is fixed in the sense of being experienced in subsequent lives.
The Discussion of Karma is finished.
The Twenty-first Chapter. Its summary (uddāna) is as follows:
"The teaching, new, has been made; is there anyone who makes the Tathāgata’s teaching new? It is possible for the Tathāgata..."
Furthermore, [the following views are held]: that one can establish a new dispensation; that an ordinary person (puthujjana) is not yet free from the karmas of the three realms;
that one can attain arahantship without having abandoned some fetters (saṃyojana); that there exists the supernormal power of intention (adhippāyiddhi) belonging to Buddhas or their disciples;
that among Buddhas there is a difference of inferiority or superiority; that Buddhas exist in all directions; that all phenomena (dhamma) are fixed; and that all karmas are fixed.
